site.alt.change.care.text: You take ownership. Your photos are on two mirrored drives in your home, so one drive failing loses nothing, and a full backup is easy: take one drive out and put a new one in, and the device copies everything onto it; the drive you took out is your backup. Nobody can reset your device password, not even us.

site.alt.change.hardware.text: You buy the hardware once. A Raspberry Pi 5 (8 GB) and two USB pen drives are all it needs. When they fill up, you swap in bigger drives instead of paying for a bigger plan.

site.alt.change.remote.text: Away from home, you need a way in. At home, the apps talk to the device directly. Elsewhere they go through our optional relay, the bridge, which is free for the first two years and then costs €9.99 + VAT a year for up to five addresses. Without it, a VPN into your home network still lets you reach your photos, and so does Tailscale Funnel for a device only you use; friends, posts, share links that work from anywhere and phone notifications need the bridge.

site.alt.change.setup.text: You set it up, once. The Mac, Windows or Linux app prepares the system card, and the setup finishes over Bluetooth from your phone, or from the Mac app: Wi-Fi, a name and a password. It takes about 20 minutes, with no terminal.

site.alt.change.title.text: What changes when you leave the cloud

site.alt.choose.ente.text: Ente if you'd rather pay for a privacy-focused photo cloud than keep a device at home: it's open source, and paid plans keep three copies in the EU.

site.alt.choose.google.text: Google Photos if you want nothing to set up or look after, and don't mind Google keeping your photos or paying for a plan once the free 15 GB fills up.

site.alt.choose.icloud.text: iCloud Photos if everyone in your family uses an iPhone or a Mac: it's built in, with nothing to set up.

site.alt.choose.immich.text: Immich if you already run a home server and are comfortable with Docker: it's a mature, free and open-source photo app.

site.alt.choose.otc.text: Off The Cloud if you want your family's photos and files at home, in full quality, with no storage plan to outgrow, on a small device that's easy to set up and needs almost no technical knowledge.

site.alt.choose.synology.text: Synology Photos if you want a ready-made NAS from an established brand that does much more than photos, and don't need the software to be open source.

site.alt.compare.checked.text: Prices checked in October 2026. Cloud prices are per month; Google One and Ente cost less paid yearly. Off The Cloud and Synology are bought once, and they also use some electricity.

site.alt.compare.lead.text: Two cloud services, three alternatives and Off The Cloud, side by side. Short answers here; the trade-offs are explained below the table.

site.alt.faq.breaks.a.text: If a drive fails, the other one holds a full copy: the device keeps working, tells you which drive to replace and fills the new one by itself. If the Raspberry Pi dies, replace it: everything is on the drives, so moving the card and the drives to a new Pi brings it back as it was. For a full backup, take one drive out and put a new one in: the drive you took out is your backup.

site.alt.faq.breaks.q.text: What happens if a drive or the Raspberry Pi breaks?

site.alt.faq.cost.a.text: It depends on how much you keep. Over five years, at October 2026 prices, iCloud+ costs €179.40 for 200 GB and €599.40 for 2 TB, and Google One's 2 TB plan €499.95 paid yearly. With Off The Cloud you buy a Raspberry Pi 5 and two USB drives once and, if you use the bridge, pay €29.97 + VAT for its third to fifth years; the device also uses some electricity. When the drives fill up, you buy bigger ones instead of a bigger plan.

site.alt.faq.cost.q.text: Is it cheaper than Google One or iCloud+?

site.alt.faq.immich.a.text: Immich is a free, open-source photo app for people who run their own server: you install it with Docker on a Linux machine and set up storage, backups and remote access yourself. Off The Cloud needs almost no technical knowledge: the app prepares a Raspberry Pi's card and the setup finishes over Bluetooth from your phone or Mac, on inexpensive hardware, a Raspberry Pi 5 and two USB pen drives. It also does more than photos: your files stay in sync with your computers, like a NAS, and a private social network connects friends' devices, which Immich doesn't have.

site.alt.faq.immich.q.text: How is it different from Immich?

site.alt.faq.private.a.text: Yes. Your photo library and files are stored encrypted on your device, with a key only your password unlocks, and the password itself is never stored on it. Tagging, place names and face recognition run on the device itself, so no photo is sent away to be analysed, and nothing is used for ads or to train AI.

site.alt.faq.side_by_side.a.text: Yes. The apps copy your photos to the device rather than moving them, so Google Photos and iCloud carry on as before and you can use both until you're sure. You can also look around the <demo>demo</demo> first: a real device with a made-up family's photos, no sign-up needed.

site.alt.faq.side_by_side.q.text: Can I try it without leaving Google Photos or iCloud?

site.alt.hero.lead.text: Off The Cloud is free, open-source software that turns a Raspberry Pi 5 into a home server for your family's photos, videos and files: it does the job of Google Photos or iCloud Photos, on a small device you own. Your phones back up your photos and videos in full quality, and the device tags them for search and keeps them on two mirrored drives, with no monthly storage plan. It suits families who would rather own a small device than pay for cloud storage every month.

site.alt.hero.title.text: A self-hosted alternative to Google Photos and iCloud

site.alt.keep.backup.text: Automatic backup from your phones. The iPhone and Android apps back up your photos and videos in the background, in full resolution, including iPhone photos kept only in iCloud.

site.alt.keep.family.text: Room for the whole family. Everyone gets their own account and password on the same device, and their photos are encrypted with their own key.

site.alt.keep.originals.text: Your originals, untouched. Each photo and video is stored as it was taken, never compressed or resized to save space.

site.alt.keep.search.text: Search and faces. Search for "beach", "dog" or a city, and browse by person and by date. Tagging, place names and face recognition all work on the device itself, and face recognition stays off until you turn it on.

site.alt.keep.sharing.text: Sharing. Send a collection to anyone as a link that expires: they open it in a browser, with no account or app. An optional private feed lets you share posts with friends you accept, with no ads or algorithm.

site.alt.move.computer.text: From a computer: the Mac, Windows and Linux apps back up any folder you choose, so photos you keep on a computer come across too.

site.alt.move.google.text: From Google Photos: the Android and iPhone apps back up the photos and videos stored on the phone, so whatever Google Photos still keeps there comes across. Photos that exist only in Google's cloud have to be downloaded to a phone or computer first.

site.alt.move.icloud.text: From iCloud Photos: install the iPhone app and, when it asks which photos to send, choose All photos and videos and leave Sync from iCloud on. The phone downloads each photo it keeps only in iCloud and sends it to your device, so a large library takes a while; keep the phone on Wi-Fi. The device gets each photo's original: edits and the moving part of Live Photos stay in iCloud, and albums aren't copied. Backing up doesn't remove anything from iCloud.
